method: Bounded Family landscape; source metadata checked via PubMed. This is not a systematic review per Driver.

BIO-F01.constructs: Sleep amount, continuity, phase, chronotype and derived sufficiency are distinct.
BIO-F01.mechanisms: Sleep and circadian phase influence waking performance with timing and baseline dependence.
BIO-F01.operations: Reuse governed sleep scheduling, CBT-I, light, melatonin and caffeine pilot operations.
BIO-F01.measurement: Sleep measures, actigraphy and specified next-day endpoints must be separated.
BIO-F01.boundaries: The governed BIO-F01 pilot is the scientific source of record; B01-B05 remain review proposals.

BIO-F02.constructs: HPA/SAM activation, autonomic arousal, recovery, reactivity and multisystem allostatic load differ.
BIO-F02.mechanisms: Acute responses and cumulative biomarker composites operate on different time scales.
BIO-F02.operations: Bounded stressor exposure and recovery observation are plausible routes.
BIO-F02.measurement: Biomarker batteries and autonomic measures are not interchangeable with felt stress.
BIO-F02.boundaries: Allostatic-load component selection varies; response-to-burden causal direction is not fixed by a biomarker correlation.

BIO-F03.constructs: Hunger, satiety, thirst, hydration, glucose and visceral signals are separate states.
BIO-F03.mechanisms: Homeostatic feedback can be anticipatory, compensatory and nonlinear.
BIO-F03.operations: Hydration, nutritional or glucose perturbations require dose, baseline and objective state verification.
BIO-F03.measurement: Osmolality, volume, glucose and reports measure different levels.
BIO-F03.boundaries: Thirst intensity is not hydration status; the controlled hypoglycemia task result in diabetes does not establish a generic fatigue Driver effect.

BIO-F04.constructs: Oxygen availability, intermittent desaturation, CO2 burden, heat and cold strain differ.
BIO-F04.mechanisms: Acute environmental exposure can alter physiology, with acclimation and task-specific responses.
BIO-F04.operations: Controlled hypoxia or thermal exposure is plausible but requires measured tissue state.
BIO-F04.measurement: Inspired gas or ambient temperature is exposure, not achieved tissue oxygen or heat strain.
BIO-F04.boundaries: Acute hypoxia and heat-acclimation reviews show task, physiological-marker and risk-of-bias heterogeneity; chronic transfer is unsupported.

BIO-F05.constructs: Physical and cognitive fatigue, acute and persistent pain, capacity and reserve differ.
BIO-F05.mechanisms: Exertion and recovery can alter fatigue while pain and capacity have distinct measurements.
BIO-F05.operations: Exercise/recovery or pain induction are plausible only at exact dose and endpoint.
BIO-F05.measurement: Subjective fatigue is not objective capacity; task failure is not a latent trait.
BIO-F05.boundaries: Exercise trials differ by chronicity and population; experimental pain can change motor strategy while task performance often remains intact.

BIO-F06.constructs: Systemic inflammatory signaling, sickness response and pathogen burden are distinct.
BIO-F06.mechanisms: Controlled inflammatory challenge can generate acute cytokine and symptom responses.
BIO-F06.operations: Experimental endotoxin is a bounded research exposure, not a practitioner action.
BIO-F06.measurement: A cytokine change alone does not measure the entire sickness response.
BIO-F06.boundaries: Endotoxin findings vary by dose and time; reviews and included challenge studies are not independent replications.

BIO-F07.constructs: Hearing, vision, olfaction, vestibular and somatosensory capacity differ from symptoms such as tinnitus.
BIO-F07.mechanisms: Sensory loss can change input and task access; compensation may mediate performance.
BIO-F07.operations: Sensory deprivation or aid manipulation requires an exact recipient and measure.
BIO-F07.measurement: Hearing threshold and cognitive test scores do not by themselves identify cognitive causation.
BIO-F07.boundaries: Most hearing-cognition evidence is observational and vulnerable to common causes and test-access artifacts.

BIO-F08.constructs: Energy sufficiency, oxygen carrying, iron, B12 and glycemic regulation are separable.
BIO-F08.mechanisms: Deficiency correction may alter fatigue within selected low-ferritin adults.
BIO-F08.operations: Iron supplementation trials offer a bounded route; treatment and achieved status remain distinct.
BIO-F08.measurement: Ferritin, hemoglobin, subjective fatigue and physical capacity are different endpoints.
BIO-F08.boundaries: Oral trials show reported-fatigue benefit; physical-capacity findings and IV routes are heterogeneous and should not be pooled as independent exact claims.

BIO-F09.constructs: Thyroid, puberty, pregnancy, menopause, reproductive hormones and sexual arousal span distinct populations and scales.
BIO-F09.mechanisms: Endocrine perturbations can have context-specific physiological and behavioral effects across life stages.
BIO-F09.operations: Replacement therapy evidence is clinical and condition-specific.
BIO-F09.measurement: TSH and free T4 are indicators; fatigue and cognition are different outcomes.
BIO-F09.boundaries: Thyroid RCT reports show no general fatigue/cognition benefit in older mild subclinical hypothyroidism; life-course synthesis does not identify one universal hormone effect.

BIO-F10.constructs: Maturation, aging burden and frailty are not chronological age itself.
BIO-F10.mechanisms: Reserve and vulnerability can alter response to stressors, but measured fitness overlaps frailty scoring.
BIO-F10.operations: Exercise in older adults is an operation, not a direct aging-mechanism intervention.
BIO-F10.measurement: Frailty, physical fitness and DNA methylation age measurements can share correlates or constituents.
BIO-F10.boundaries: Meta-analytic associations among frailty, fitness and methylation clocks do not identify independent causal directions; puberty-related white matter maturation is separate.

BIO-F11.constructs: Polygenic liability is a predictive susceptibility profile, not an acute state.
BIO-F11.mechanisms: Variants may contribute to risk through many downstream mechanisms.
BIO-F11.operations: No routine acute manipulation of the profile is scientifically coherent.
BIO-F11.measurement: Portability and ancestry affect score calibration and meaning.
BIO-F11.boundaries: Prediction, ancestry transfer and mechanism cannot be collapsed into a manipulable causal Driver claim.

BIO-F12.constructs: Traumatic injury, encephalopathy, postictal, focal and neurodegenerative impairment differ.
BIO-F12.mechanisms: Injury and disease may impair domain-specific function with severity and recovery dependence.
BIO-F12.operations: Clinical exposure is not a reusable recommended operation.
BIO-F12.measurement: Cognitive tests measure outcomes, not the whole neurological state.
BIO-F12.boundaries: TBI longitudinal syntheses show heterogeneous courses; Alzheimer biological subtypes further warn against a single neurodegenerative trajectory.

BIO-F13.constructs: Alcohol, THC, nicotine, caffeine, sedative, opioid, stimulant and medication burdens are realized effects, not administered doses.
BIO-F13.mechanisms: Pharmacology depends on dose, tolerance, timing, formulation and interactions.
BIO-F13.operations: Administration identities must be distinct from realized biological effect.
BIO-F13.measurement: Working-memory and driving-related task impairment are not broad functional capacity.
BIO-F13.boundaries: Alcohol and THC syntheses show dose, task, timing and user-history moderation; neither licenses a universal capacity edge.

BIO-F14.constructs: Dependence, cessation and each substance-specific withdrawal syndrome are distinct.
BIO-F14.mechanisms: Abrupt caffeine cessation after regular intake can produce time-bounded withdrawal with variable incidence.
BIO-F14.operations: Blinded placebo substitution is a coherent research operation; it cannot stand for nicotine, cannabis, alcohol or opioid cessation.
BIO-F14.measurement: Syndrome severity requires symptoms over a window; headache alone is only a component.
BIO-F14.boundaries: Caffeine, cannabis, nicotine and opioid withdrawal have different populations and measurement; selected symptomatic samples and general samples yield different incidence.
